EV-0680.extract_label: Extract from the letter of 9 October 2026 (verbatim; the requester's name and contact details are withheld)
EV-0680.extract: We have conducted searches for information in relation to yourself at our storage facility and on all Defence Business Services systems using the information you have provided, no information in scope of your request was located.

p: Defence Business Services (DBS) searched its storage facility and all DBS systems for information about the requester and located nothing in scope. No exemption is cited, so this is a plain "not held" answer, not a refusal.

sections.h: What a "not held" answer means, and does not mean
li: It means the holder found nothing on the systems it searched, on the date it searched. It is a statement about those records, not about the events of 1988.

A subject access request reaches personal data about the requester. Deployment orders, Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA) files or correspondence with the police and the Welsh Office that never name the requester would fall outside it, even if they exist.

The searches named are DBS storage and DBS systems (the civilian disclosure team). The letter does not state whether operational or Army records held elsewhere in the Ministry of Defence, or records already transferred to The National Archives, were searched.

sections.h: Read against hindsight and the wider record
li: EV-0192 (MOD internal review of FOI2026/09190, 10 October 2026) passed the personal-information parts of the earlier FOI request on for subject access handling. This letter is the outcome of that strand, so the FOI and the SAR now answer different questions: the FOI asked about information in general, the SAR about information on the requester.

The earlier FOI response (FOI2026/09019, 29 May 2026) gave a neither-confirm-nor-deny answer under section 23(5) for the Special Forces parts and "not held" for the rest. A "not held" answer under subject access does not reopen or settle that section 23(5) position.

The Health and Safety Executive's reply under the Environmental Information Regulations (EIR 2026/224580, 5 November 2026) also returned "not held" for 1988–89 records, explaining a seven-year retention period and no transfer or disposal records. Together these show a pattern of 1988-era records not being found by the bodies asked; whether that reflects routine retention, records held elsewhere, or records never made is the open question.

sections.h: What cuts against reading more into it
li: A civil possession in 1988 would ordinarily be carried out by court officers with police support; no involvement by the Armed Forces is the ordinary expectation, and an empty search is what that expectation predicts.
MACA tasking for a civil eviction would be unusual, and the absence of any trace in the searched systems is consistent with there having been none.
Nothing in this letter points to concealment: it is prompt, cites no exemption and gives the routes onward.
An internal review by the MOD Information Rights Compliance Team, asking which record systems beyond DBS were searched and under what terms.
If the review does not answer that, a complaint to the Information Commissioner under section 165 of the Data Protection Act 2018.
A search of The National Archives' defence and Welsh Office series for 1988–89 for any record of support to the civil authorities at Llandough.
